description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, renowned for its comforting warmth and rich, earthy flavor. This hearty and nutritious soup is a staple in Turkish cuisine, often served with a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of spicy butter. It is incredibly easy to prepare, offering a taste of authentic Turkey right in your kitchen.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear; drain well. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic cloves. Have all other ingredients measured and ready.

instructions.title: Sauté the Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Flour, Tomato Paste, and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the all-purpose flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux. Add the tomato paste, dried mint, and red pepper flakes, stirring for another minute until fragrant and well combined with the onion mixture.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water), stirring well to prevent lumps. Season with salt and black pepper.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Prepare Spiced Butter (Optional)
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add an additional 1/2 teaspoon of dried mint and 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (pul biber). Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. This will be drizzled over the soup when serving.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving with the spiced butter, if using, and garnish with fresh lemon wedges on the side. Serve immediately with crusty bread for a truly comforting meal.

tips: For a truly authentic touch, always serve Mercimek Corbasi with a wedge of fresh lemon and a drizzle of melted butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber). The acidity of the lemon brightens the soup, and the spiced butter adds a wonderful aroma and gentle heat.

Rinsing the red lentils thoroughly before cooking is crucial to remove any impurities and ensure a clear, flavorful broth. If you prefer a smoother soup, use an immersion blender directly in the pot; otherwise, carefully transfer batches to a regular blender.

Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if it has thickened too much.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi, or Turkish Red Lentil Soup, is more than just a dish; it’s a warm embrace in a bowl, a staple of Turkish cuisine that transcends meal times. From bustling Istanbul street vendors to cozy family kitchens across Anatolia, this vibrant, creamy soup holds a special place in the hearts and bellies of millions. Its comforting simplicity, combined with a rich depth of flavor, makes it an irresistible choice for any occasion. Whether you’re seeking a nourishing breakfast, a light lunch, or a hearty starter for dinner, Mercimek Corbasi offers a delightful experience that’s both satisfying and incredibly easy to prepare.

This humble yet flavorful soup is renowned for its wholesome ingredients and the beautiful, earthy aroma that fills the kitchen as it simmers. It’s a testament to how basic components can be transformed into something truly extraordinary with a little care and the right balance of spices. If you’ve ever found yourself captivated by the diverse and delectable world of Turkish soups and stews, Mercimek Corbasi is undoubtedly a dish you must master.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi is a traditional Turkish soup primarily made from red lentils. Its name directly translates to "lentil soup," highlighting its main ingredient. It’s characterized by its smooth, velvety texture and its distinct reddish-orange hue, often brightened further by a swirl of spiced butter or oil. This soup is a cornerstone of Turkish culinary culture, frequently served as a starter but equally popular as a light main course, especially during colder months or for a quick, nutritious meal.

The essence of Turkish Red Lentil Soup lies in its simplicity and the masterful combination of a few key ingredients. Red lentils, known for their quick cooking time and creamy consistency when puréed, form the base. They are typically simmered with aromatic vegetables like onions and carrots, a touch of tomato paste for depth, and a blend of spices, most notably dried mint and paprika or chili flakes. The result is a wonderfully savory, slightly earthy soup that is both incredibly filling and surprisingly light. It’s a dish that embodies warmth, comfort, and the rustic charm of Turkish home cooking.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Crafting an authentic bowl of Mercimek Corbasi requires a handful of readily available ingredients. The beauty of this soup lies in its straightforward nature, allowing the natural flavors to shine through.

For the soup base:
*   **Red Lentils:** Approximately 1 cup (200g). These are the star of the show, providing the creamy texture and earthy flavor. Ensure they are thoroughly rinsed.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Adds a foundational sweetness and aromatic base.
*   **Carrot:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Contributes natural sweetness and helps build a complex flavor profile.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced (optional, but highly recommended for depth).
*   **Tomato Paste:** 1-2 tablespoons. Provides umami, color, and a subtle tang.
*   **Vegetable or Chicken Broth:** 6-8 cups (1.5-2 liters). The liquid base; broth adds more flavor than just water.
*   **Water:** If needed, to adjust consistency.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** 2 tablespoons, for sautéing vegetables.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste.

For the vibrant topping (Nane Yağı - Mint Butter):
*   **Butter:** 2 tablespoons (unsalted is best). This creates a rich, flavorful base for the spices.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons. Essential for the classic Turkish aroma and flavor. Do not skip this!
*   **Aleppo Pepper (Pul Biber) or Paprika:** 1-2 teaspoons. Adds a beautiful red color and a mild, pleasant warmth. Adjust to your spice preference.

These ingredients, when combined, create the quintessential Turkish Red Lentil Soup experience.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Mercimek Corbasi

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a rewarding culinary journey that yields delicious results. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any impurities and excess starch, which can cause the soup to become cloudy. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the chopped carrot and minced garlic (if using), and continue to cook for another 5 minutes until the carrots begin to soften.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Spices:** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step helps to deepen the flavor of the tomato paste. Add a pinch of salt and black pepper at this stage.
4.  **Combine Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the sautéed vegetables and tomato paste. Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend the Soup:** Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it’s smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer batches of the soup to a regular blender and blend until smooth. Be cautious when blending hot liquids. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning (salt and pepper) as needed.
6.  **Prepare the Mint Butter Topping (Nane Yağı):** While the soup is simmering or after blending, melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foaming, remove it from the heat and stir in the dried mint and Aleppo pepper (or paprika). The residual heat will warm the spices without burning them, releasing their fragrant aromas.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a generous amount of the spiced mint butter over each serving. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving the perfect Mercimek Corbasi is simple, but a few expert tips can elevate your soup from good to truly outstanding.

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This cannot be stressed enough. Rinsing removes starches that can make your soup gummy or cloudy. Keep rinsing until the water runs clear.
*   **Sauté Vegetables Until Soft:** Don’t rush the sautéing process. Allowing the onions and carrots to soften and slightly caramelize builds a crucial flavor foundation for your Turkish Red Lentil Soup.
*   **Toast the Tomato Paste:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding liquids deepens its flavor and removes any raw taste, contributing to a richer, more complex soup.
*   **Don't Skip the Mint Butter:** The *nane yağı* is not just a garnish; it's an integral part of the Mercimek Corbasi experience. The aromatic dried mint infused in butter with a touch of chili flake adds a burst of flavor and a beautiful visual element that truly makes the soup sing.
*   **Adjust Consistency to Your Liking:** Some prefer a thicker, heartier soup, while others prefer it slightly thinner. Feel free to add more hot broth or water after blending to achieve your ideal consistency. Remember, it will thicken slightly as it cools.
*   **Let It Rest (Optional but Recommended):** Like many soups, Mercimek Corbasi often tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions for Mercimek Corbasi

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments.

*   **Lemon Wedges:** This is non-negotiable! A squeeze of fresh lemon juice over your bowl of Turkish Red Lentil Soup brightens all the flavors and adds a zesty tang that cuts through the richness, creating a perfectly balanced taste.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A slice of fresh, crusty bread (like a baguette or Turkish pide) is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the delicious soup.
*   **Extra Chili Flakes:** For those who enjoy a bit more heat, a sprinkle of extra *pul biber* (Aleppo pepper) or red pepper flakes can be added to individual servings.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** While the dried mint butter is classic, a scattering of fresh parsley or cilantro can add a touch of freshness and color.
*   **Yogurt:** While not traditionally served with Mercimek Corbasi, a small dollop of plain yogurt or a spoonful of crème fraîche can add a creamy, cooling contrast, especially if you’ve made your soup extra spicy.
*   **As a Starter:** Mercimek Corbasi is often served as the first course in a larger Turkish meal, preceding kebabs, stews, or other main dishes.
*   **As a Light Meal:** With its wholesome ingredients and satisfying texture, it also makes a complete and nourishing light lunch or dinner on its own.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is beloved for a reason, there are several ways to adapt it to your preferences or dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** This soup is naturally vegetarian. To make it vegan, simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth, and use olive oil or a plant-based butter alternative for both the sautéing and the spiced topping.
*   **Added Vegetables:** Feel free to incorporate other vegetables for extra nutrients and flavor. A small diced potato can add extra body, while celery or bell peppers can introduce different aromatic notes. Add them along with the onions and carrots.
*   **Spicier Kick:** If you love heat, increase the amount of Aleppo pepper or use a spicier variety of chili flakes in the mint butter topping. You could also add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the soup base while it simmers.
*   **Different Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, a sprinkle of fresh dill or flat-leaf parsley stirred in at the end can offer a different aromatic profile. However, the dried mint is truly what gives it its authentic Turkish character.
*   **Texture Preferences:** If you prefer a slightly chunkier soup, you can blend only half of the soup or blend it less thoroughly, leaving some small pieces of lentils and vegetables.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Mercimek Corbasi is naturally gluten-free, making it an excellent option for those with gluten sensitivities. Just ensure your broth is also gluten-free.

No matter how you choose to prepare or enjoy it, Mercimek Corbasi remains a testament to the comforting power of simple, wholesome ingredients. This Turkish Red Lentil Soup is not just food; it's a taste of tradition, warmth, and hospitality. Its ease of preparation and deeply satisfying flavor make it a beloved dish that deserves a permanent spot in your culinary repertoire. Give it a try, and you’ll quickly understand why this vibrant red lentil soup is a Turkish national treasure.
